statement.text:
Let G be a group generated by 3 class transpositions (see the definition in
17.57), and let m be the least common multiple of the moduli of the residue classes
interchanged by the generators of G. Assume that G does not setwisely stabilize any
union of residue classes modulo m except for ∅ and Z, and assume that the integers
0, 1, . . . , 42 all lie in the same orbit under the action of G on Z. Is the action of G
on N ∪ {0} necessarily transitive?
    The bound 42 cannot be replaced by a smaller number, since the finite group
⟨τ0(2),1(2) , τ0(3),2(3) , τ0(7),6(7) ⟩ acts transitively on the set {0, . . . , 41}, as well as on the
set of residue classes modulo 42.                                                               S. Kohl
